_comment: Copy to config/profile.json and replace every value with your own. profile.json is gitignored — it holds your salary floor, work authorisation and the evidence the model is allowed to claim on your behalf. This file is a WORKING example: the shapes matter, and the tool will run unchanged against it, but the answers will be someone else's.
name: Ada Example
headline: Full-stack engineer — payments, integrations, production LLM systems
summary: Two sentences in your own words: what you build, and what you have run in production. The scorer reads this before anything else, so vague self-description here costs accuracy on every role.

seniority._comment: acceptTitles earns the titleMatchBonus in the prescore. rejectTitles is matched before scoring, so anything here is a role you will never be shown.

stack._comment: term is matched case-insensitively against title + description; weight is points added, capped per bucket by rules.prescore.max*Points. Keep terms short and lowercase. These three buckets are the whole keyword half of the prescore.

evidence: One line per thing you actually shipped, with a number in it where you have one.
The model may only draw on these when it writes a cover letter — if it is not here, it cannot claim it.
Cut anything you would not want quoted back at you in an interview.

workAuth.note: Stated verbatim in application answers. Roughly 38% of otherwise-matching remote roles die here rather than on skill, so being precise costs nothing and saves the model from guessing.

compensation.note: Used to reason about a posting's stated range. Never written into an application answer.

neverClaim._comment: A hard gate, not a hint. If a generated application contains one of these terms, the whole kit is REJECTED rather than edited — a model asked to describe you against a posting will happily borrow the posting's stack. A false claim survives the screen and collapses at the first interview question. List anything a job ad might tempt it into.

terms.truth: Never run it. Deploys are on managed platforms.
